claims.text: Adding tungsten powder to a CoCrFeNi coating causes tungsten-based phases to form within the coating microstructure.
The tungsten-based phases may include tungsten oxides.
Tungsten-derived phases develop a lubricious tribolayer during high-temperature sliding.
At elevated temperatures, tungsten reacts to form stable lubricious compounds.
The tungsten-derived compounds reduce interfacial shear stress.
Reduced interfacial shear stress decreases friction.
Formation of the tungsten-derived lubricious phase decreases wear.
Tungsten's high-temperature stability and lubricity stabilize tribological performance over a broad temperature range.
The tungsten-added CoCrFeNi coating will have a lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
The tungsten-added CoCrFeNi coating will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi coatings exhibit increased friction and wear variability over the tested temperature range.
The intervention is effective at loads comparable to those used in prior tribological studies.
Sufficient environmental oxygen is required to enable the tungsten oxidation associated with the proposed benefit.
The tribological benefits diminish when the tungsten content is too low.
The tribological benefits diminish outside the studied temperature and load range.
The optimal tungsten concentration and precise identity of the tungsten-derived phases remain undetermined.
